content_voiceover: This is the pivotal TOWER trial, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in twenty seventeen, comparing blinatumomab to standard chemotherapy in relapsed or refractory Philadelphia chromosome negative ALL. Overall survival was significantly longer with blinatumomab, a median of seven point seven months versus four months with chemotherapy, a hazard ratio of point seven one, p equals point zero one, an absolute gain of three point seven months highlighted right on the slide. Event free survival showed an even more dramatic relative benefit, with a hazard ratio of point five five and six month event free survival estimates of thirty one percent for blinatumomab against just twelve percent for chemotherapy. The response table below breaks down hematologic outcomes at twelve weeks, complete remission with full hematologic recovery was achieved in thirty three point six percent of the blinatumomab group versus fifteen point seven percent with chemotherapy, and when you include partial or incomplete recovery, complete remission rates were forty three point nine versus twenty four point six percent, both differences highly significant. This is the trial that put blinatumomab on the map for boards, remember the numbers, roughly double the remission rate and nearly double the median overall survival compared to salvage chemotherapy in relapsed refractory Ph negative ALL.
keypoints: TOWER trial, NEJM 2017, relapsed/refractory Ph- ALL
Median OS 7.7 vs 4.0 months, HR 0.71, gain of 3.7 months
CR with full hematologic recovery 33.6% vs 15.7%
keypoint_voiceover: TOWER established blinatumomab over chemotherapy in relapsed refractory Ph negative ALL: median overall survival nearly doubled from four to seven point seven months, and complete remission with full recovery roughly doubled too, thirty four percent versus sixteen percent.
